To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) the MDR hamster cell line exhibits several alterations of gene expression, and that (ii) the P-glyco-protein associated MDR can be modulated by cyclosporin-A and BSO.

the MDR hamster CHO cell subline exhibits a complex pattern of altered gene expression and that the MDR phenotype is not only associated with the P-glyco protein, but also with a reduced glutathione-S- transferase-P gene expression and the appearance of a novel 15.5kDa protein.

the MDR CHO cell line exhibits an altered gene expression profile with respect to the expression of the P-170 gene and several other genes and that this MDR subline shows a pronounced collateral sensitivity towards the dihydropyri dine anticancer drug dexinguldipine-HCI, a rather hydrophobic drug not usually involved in P-gp associated MDR.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a multidrug-resistant cell line exhibiting several alterations in the gene expression of proteins which are involved in drug metabolism and drug resistance.
the identification of novel MDR mechanisms, the development of MDR modulation strategies and the elucidation of the underlying molecular basis.
the characterization of the MDR sublines in terms of their altered gene expression, and the effects of the immunosuppressants cyclosporin and BSO on their MDR phenotype.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

MDR in this particular hamster cell system is a multifactorial process involving at least the expression of the P-170 glycoprotein and sorcins, the topoisomerase I and II levels, the glutathione-S- transferase-P gene expression and the appearance of a 15 kDa protein.
the MDR hamster subline is not a typical MDR cell line but rather a model system for the study of multidrug resistance.
this MDR subline exhibits multiple altered gene expression which can be influenced in different ways by various agents.

the MDR sublines showed multiple gene expression alterations, including a lowered glutathione S-transferase-P gene and topoisomerase-II protein expression and the emergence of a new 15.5-kDa protein, which might be a marker for a new MDR phenotype, and a lowered sensitivity to the anticancer drug bleomycin, which is usually not involved in the P-glycprotein-associated MDR.
MDR is a multifactorial process involving a number of genes and proteins, which can be modulated by different drugs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MDR sublines studied here exhibit a complex pattern of alterations in gene expression and drug sensitivities.
the MDR sublines may serve as an interesting model to study the effects of drugs on gene expression and to evaluate new agents for their MDR reversing properties.
the MDR phenotype of this cell system can be influenced by a number of agents, including B859-35, which is a new lead structure for MDR modulators.
